mechanism_narrative: The recent rise in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES indicates more commuting and daytime activity, which should lift discretionary visits to shops and leisure venues over the next month.
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next 28 days while TRANSIT and WORKPLACES remain above their t-2w levels, this mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL stays elevated and TRANSIT remains deeply negative, households substitute away from out-of-home shopping, keeping retail-and-recreation mobility flat to lower over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains below -35 while RESIDENTIAL stays above +7
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC rises over the next 14 days despite TRANSIT staying below -35 and RESIDENTIAL staying above +7, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rebound in PARKS is an early sign of broader outing intensity, and after a short lag it spills into retail and recreation visits.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises above 0 after two consecutive weekly increases
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC does not improve within one week after PARKS crosses above 0 and keeps rising, reject this hypothesis.

mechanism_narrative: If GROCERY_PHARM remains much less negative than RETAIL_REC, households are still making essential trips but not discretionary trips, so retail mobility will continue to lag over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RETAIL_REC stays at least 15 points below GROCERY_PHARM
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC narrows the gap to GROCERY_PHARM by more than 10 points and then rises over the next 28 days, this claim is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent upswing in PARKS combined with only a mild recovery in TRANSIT signals weather-driven outdoor substitution rather than shopping normalization, which suppresses retail-and-recreation mobility over the next month.
candidate_trigger: PARKS is positive for two straight weeks while TRANSIT stays below -30
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days while PARKS stays positive and TRANSIT remains below -30, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A gradual improvement in TRANSIT reduces trip friction and increases incidental shopping opportunities, so retail-and-recreation mobility should move up within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT improves by at least 3 points week-on-week
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC does not rise within 14 days after TRANSIT improves by at least 3 points week-on-week, reject the hypothesis.

mechanism_narrative: Because WORKPLACES is still deeply negative while RESIDENTIAL is stable and positive, daytime circulation remains incomplete; retail-and-recreation mobility will stay below the previous four-week average.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES remains below -30 while RESIDENTIAL stays above +7
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES stays below -30 and RESIDENTIAL stays above +7 yet RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Once GROCERY_PHARM approaches its baseline while RETAIL_REC remains depressed, residents are reallocating trips toward essentials rather than discretionary destinations, implying another short-term decline in retail mobility.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises above -15 while RETAIL_REC stays below -25
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC increases within 7 days after GROCERY_PHARM rises above -15 while RETAIL_REC remains below -25, the hypothesis fails.
